data.title: Express Entry Programs
data.subtitle: Your fast-track pathway to permanent residency in Canada—built for skilled professionals like you.
data.intro_title: Move to Canada as a Skilled Worker
data.intro_description: Canada's Express Entry system is one of the fastest and most competitive immigration pathways for skilled workers. Whether you're applying under the Canadian Experience Class (CEC), Federal Skilled Worker Program (FSW), or Federal Skilled Trades Program (FST), Velox Immigration helps you navigate every stage—from profile creation to receiving your permanent resident visa.
data.intro_cta_text: Book Consultation to Check Your Eligibility
data.who_we_help_intro: You may qualify under Express Entry if you are:

who_we_help_items.title: Federal Skilled Worker (FSW)
who_we_help_items.description:
For skilled workers with foreign work experience

  • Minimum 1 year skilled work experience
  • Language proficiency (CLB 7)
  • Education assessment (ECA)

who_we_help_items.title: Canadian Experience Class (CEC)
who_we_help_items.description:
For recent graduates with Canadian experience

  • 1 year Canadian work experience
  • Language proficiency (CLB 7 for NOC 0/A, CLB 5 for B)

who_we_help_items.title: Federal Skilled Trades (FST)
who_we_help_items.description:
For qualified tradespersons

  •  2 years work experience in a skilled trade
  • Language proficiency (CLB 5)
  • Valid job offer or certification

who_we_help_subitems.item: PR-ready candidates with strong language skills, education, and job experience

data.what_we_offer_intro: Velox Immigration provides end-to-end support through each step of the Express Entry journey:

what_we_offer_items.title: Express Entry Profile Creation
what_we_offer_items.description: We assess your eligibility and prepare your online profile, ensuring accurate entry of education, work history, language results (IELTS/CELPIP/TEF), and National Occupation Classification (NOC) codes.

what_we_offer_items.title: Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) Optimization
what_we_offer_items.description: We help you improve your CRS score by exploring job offers, provincial nominations, education equivalency (ECA), and language retesting strategies.

what_we_offer_items.title: Permanent Residence Application After ITA
what_we_offer_items.description: Once you receive an Invitation to Apply (ITA), we help you gather and submit all required documentation—proof of work experience, police clearances, medical exams, and more—within the 60-day window.

data.what_you_need_intro: To enter the Express Entry pool, you typically need:

description_items.description: Language test results (IELTS/CELPIP for English, TEF for French)
Educational Credential Assessment (ECA) if your education is from outside Canada
At least 1 year of skilled work experience (in Canada or abroad)
Job offer or PNP nomination (if applicable)
Proof of funds to support yourself and family in Canada
Civil status documents (marriage certificates, birth certificates)

faq_items.question: What's a competitive CRS score for an invitation?
faq_items.answer: CRS score cutoffs vary with each draw. In recent general draws, scores between 470-490 have been competitive for Federal Skilled Worker (FSW) and Canadian Experience Class (CEC) candidates. Program-specific or PNP draws may have different thresholds. Our team monitors these trends and helps optimize your profile to meet or exceed current requirements.

faq_items.question: Can I include my spouse and children in my application?
faq_items.answer: Yes, your spouse or common-law partner and dependent children can be included as accompanying dependents on your Express Entry application. Your spouse's factors (like language skills and education) can provide additional points to your CRS score. Dependent children are typically those under 22 years of age who don't have a spouse and are financially dependent on you.

faq_items.question: What if my CRS score isn't high enough for an ITA?
faq_items.answer:
If your CRS score isn't competitive, we'll work with you on multiple strategies to improve it:

Pursuing Provincial Nominee Programs (adds 600 points)
Improving language test scores (up to 310 points)
Gaining additional Canadian work experience
Adding education credentials or Canadian education
Exploring alternative immigration programs outside Express Entry

faq_items.question: Does Express Entry guarantee permanent residency?
faq_items.answer: No. Being in the Express Entry pool doesn't guarantee an invitation to apply, and receiving an ITA doesn't guarantee approval. Your application must be complete, accurate, and meet all eligibility requirements. Additionally, you must pass medical, security, and background checks. Our expertise ensures your application is properly prepared to maximize chances of approval once invited.

faq_items.question: What is the typical processing time for Express Entry?
faq_items.answer: IRCC aims to process most Express Entry applications within 6 months from the date a complete application is submitted after receiving an ITA. However, processing times can vary based on application volume, completeness of your submission, verification requirements, and other factors. Our detailed approach to application preparation helps minimize delays that could extend this timeframe.
